purpose: Compare the frozen reader implementation with the Veritas branch reader on an identical sealed public-recording range without touching the running campaign.

changes: Tail.refresh caches the finalized/open segment path list while the source directory device, inode, mtime_ns and ctime_ns remain unchanged; directory changes trigger a rescan and symlink check.
Engine.consume returns decoded frame events so Context.consume reuses them for last-trade tracking.

refresh_baseline.method: Forced full directory refresh over 6134 segment paths.

refresh_cached.method: 100 forced refresh calls with unchanged directory metadata after initial listing.

limitations: The performance replay measures Tail plus Context, not the complete Shadow.consume path with follow-up scans, policy inference, SQLite writes and status checkpoints.
The bounded range begins mid-campaign, so its 16 checkpoint rows were omitted from Context replay; Tail independently verified the 16 sealed segment hashes through the endpoint.
The CPU-quota calculation extrapolates a forced-refresh microbenchmark at the configured 0.5-second refresh interval; it is not a long-run service profile.
No throughput, decision freshness or economic outcome has been measured on the running frozen worker.
